mistakes.prevent: Rotate the input shaft gently as it enters so the rings compress into their grooves.

mistakes.title: Drum not fully engaged
mistakes.what: Leaves the forward drum sitting on its splines instead of fully down.
mistakes.consequence: Parts bind or are crushed when the case and housing go on over them.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the drum until it drops, and check the stack height matches what you saw at teardown.

steps.title: Orient and fit the sun gear
steps.action: Fit the sun gear with the side carrying the full-circle oil slot toward the drum and the three-slot side toward the planet.
steps.why: Backward, it cuts off lube oil to the planetary.
steps.mistake: Installing the sun gear backward and starving the planet of oil.

mistakes.title: Sun gear installed backward
mistakes.what: Fits the sun gear with the three-slot side toward the drum.
mistakes.consequence: Lube oil to the planetary is cut off, and the planets fail and shed debris through the unit.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the full-circle slot toward the drum and the three-slot side toward the planet.

steps.title: Fit the planet and ring gear
steps.action: Install the planet carrier and ring gear, turning them until the splines drop in.

mistakes.title: Hammering the splines together
mistakes.what: Taps the planet carrier or ring gear down with a mallet instead of turning it into mesh.
mistakes.consequence: Splines or thrust faces are burred, and the planetary binds or wears early.
mistakes.prevent: Rotate the carrier and ring gear until the splines drop in under their own weight.

steps.title: Install the reverse brake housing
steps.action: Set the reverse brake pack and housing over the planetary, torque the housing support bolts, then fit the separator plate and internal manual valve body.

mistakes.title: Pinching the reverse pack
mistakes.what: Lowers the reverse brake housing with plate lugs out of line with their slots.
mistakes.consequence: A plate lug breaks or the reverse pack binds under the housing.
mistakes.prevent: Align the reverse plate lugs with the housing slots and let it drop without force.

mistakes.title: Separator plate flipped
mistakes.what: Fits the separator plate under the internal manual valve the wrong way up.
mistakes.consequence: Forward or reverse feed is blocked and the case has to come off again.
mistakes.prevent: Follow the mark made at teardown and check the plate holes line up with the passages.

mistakes.title: Uneven housing support torque
mistakes.what: Tightens the six housing support bolts one at a time to full torque.
mistakes.consequence: The housing distorts and the reverse piston binds in its bore.
mistakes.prevent: Snug all six support bolts first, then tighten them in a crossing pattern.

steps.title: Seat the secondary pulley
steps.action: Put the original or newly selected rear shims in place, lower the secondary pulley in and fit its retaining bolts.
steps.mistake: Leaving out or swapping a rear shim, which shifts the pulley and misaligns the chain.

mistakes.title: Rear shim omitted or swapped
mistakes.what: Leaves out a secondary rear shim or uses the primary pulley's shim.
mistakes.consequence: The pulley sits in the wrong axial position and the chain runs misaligned, wearing chain and pulleys.
mistakes.prevent: Refit the labelled shims, or newly selected ones, and recheck the stack before lowering the pulley.

mistakes.title: Uneven pulley retaining bolts
mistakes.what: Tightens the three secondary pulley bolts one at a time.
mistakes.consequence: The bearing retainer cocks and the secondary pulley sits crooked in the case.
mistakes.prevent: Snug all three secondary pulley bolts, then tighten them evenly in turn.

steps.title: Open the secondary pulley again
steps.action: Refit the expander tool and open the secondary pulley evenly until the chain can be fitted.

mistakes.title: Opening the pulley unevenly
mistakes.what: Tightens one side of the expander ahead of the other during assembly.
mistakes.consequence: The sheave cocks on its shaft, or the tool slips and slams the sheave shut.
mistakes.prevent: Alternate small turns on the expander and check the sheave gap is even on both sides.

steps.title: Hang chain and primary pulley
steps.action: With its front bearing shim fitted, tip the primary pulley in with the chain on both pulleys in its marked direction, fit the right chain guide, then stand the pulley up and bolt it in.
steps.why: The right guide only goes in while the primary pulley is tipped.
steps.mistake: Fitting a reused chain reversed, so worn surfaces meet fresh ones.

mistakes.title: Reused chain fitted reversed
mistakes.what: Fits a reused variator chain opposite its marked running direction.
mistakes.consequence: Surfaces that wore in one way are loaded the other way, bringing noise and faster wear.
mistakes.prevent: Follow the paint arrow when fitting a reused chain, or fit a new chain instead.

mistakes.title: Forgetting the primary front shim
mistakes.what: Tips the primary pulley in without its front bearing shim.
mistakes.consequence: The primary sits out of position and the chain runs misaligned between the pulleys.
mistakes.prevent: Fit and check the primary front bearing shim before the pulley goes in.

mistakes.title: Chain not seated on both sheaves
mistakes.what: Leaves the chain riding the rim of one pulley.
mistakes.consequence: When the expander is released the chain is pinched and damaged.
mistakes.prevent: Check the chain sits fully between the sheaves of both pulleys before standing the primary up.

mistakes.title: Right guide left out
mistakes.what: Stands the primary pulley up before fitting the right chain guide.
mistakes.consequence: The right guide can't go in afterward, so the pulley has to be unbolted and tipped again.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the right chain guide while the primary pulley is still tipped toward the secondary.

steps.title: Lock the chain guides together
steps.action: Join the guide halves around the chain until all locking tabs click, then fit the guide anchor bolt.

mistakes.title: Guide tabs not fully locked
mistakes.what: Closes the guide halves but leaves one locking tab not fully clicked.
mistakes.consequence: The guide can come apart in service and the chain then rubs the oil tubes, losing pressure.
mistakes.prevent: Check each of the four guide tabs by eye and feel after closing the guide.

mistakes.title: Anchor bolt left out
mistakes.what: Forgets to refit the chain guide anchor bolt.
mistakes.consequence: The guide moves with the chain, wears quickly and can break apart.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the guide anchor bolt before the expander is released.

steps.title: Release the pulley onto the chain
steps.action: Back the expander tool off slowly and evenly, watching the chain pull into both pulleys, then turn the pulleys by hand.
steps.why: A sudden release lets the spring slam the sheaves onto a misplaced chain.

mistakes.title: Releasing the expander quickly
mistakes.what: Backs the expander off fast or one side at a time.
mistakes.consequence: The spring slams the sheaves onto a chain that may not be fully seated.
mistakes.prevent: Release the expander evenly in small turns, watching the chain pull into both pulleys.

mistakes.title: Not turning the pulleys by hand
mistakes.what: Skips rotating the pulleys after the expander is released.
mistakes.consequence: A misplaced chain or a rubbing guide is found only after the case is closed.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the pulleys through several turns and watch the chain and guides before the case goes on.

steps.title: Refit the pulley baffle
steps.action: Bolt the baffle back around the secondary pulley.

mistakes.title: Baffle rubbing the pulley
mistakes.what: Bolts on a bent secondary pulley baffle or one that isn't seated.
mistakes.consequence: The baffle rubs the secondary pulley, making noise and debris.
mistakes.prevent: Check the baffle's shape, fit it square and turn the pulley to check it clears.

steps.title: Lower on the transmission case
steps.action: Clean both case faces dry, lay an even bead of Subaru-specified liquid gasket, then lower the case straight down over the pulley shafts without disturbing the chain.

mistakes.title: Sealant on oily case faces
mistakes.what: Lays the case bead on faces that are not completely clean and dry.
mistakes.consequence: The liquid gasket doesn't bond to the oily aluminum and the case-half seam leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Degrease and dry both case faces right before the bead goes on.

mistakes.title: Too heavy a case bead
mistakes.what: Runs a thick bead of liquid gasket on the case face.
mistakes.consequence: Excess squeezes into the case where it can block passages or the strainer.
mistakes.prevent: Lay a small even bead on the case face, enough to seal but not to squeeze inward.

mistakes.title: Case passage O-rings left out
mistakes.what: Lowers the case without the two O-rings that seal its passages.
mistakes.consequence: A hydraulic circuit leaks inside the unit and the case has to come off again.
mistakes.prevent: Check both new case passage O-rings are in place before lowering the case.

mistakes.title: Sealant skinned before assembly
mistakes.what: Lays the case bead and then gets held up before the case goes on.
mistakes.consequence: Skinned sealant doesn't wet the other face, so the joint leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Have the case ready to lower before the bead goes on and close the joint promptly.

mistakes.title: Knocking the chain with the case
mistakes.what: Lowers the case tilted so it hits the chain or a guide.
mistakes.consequence: A guide tab breaks or the chain is displaced without anyone seeing it.
mistakes.prevent: Lower the case level and slowly over the pulley shafts, watching the chain.

steps.title: Torque the case-half bolts
steps.action: Run the case bolts down and torque them to spec in a crossing pattern.

mistakes.title: Pulling the case down unevenly
mistakes.what: Tightens the case-half bolts one side at a time.
mistakes.consequence: The case distorts, bearing bores misalign and the seam leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Snug all the case bolts, then torque them in a crossing pattern in stages.

mistakes.title: Not checking rotation after torque
mistakes.what: Torques the case without turning the input shaft and pulleys.
mistakes.consequence: A bind is discovered only after the unit is installed in the car.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the input shaft by hand after torquing and feel for any tight spot.

mistakes.title: Stripping case threads
mistakes.what: Over-tightens a case bolt or uses the wrong bolt in a hole.
mistakes.consequence: The aluminum thread in the converter case strips and needs a thread insert before assembly can go on.
mistakes.prevent: Use the bolt that came out of that hole and tighten it with a torque wrench.

steps.title: Install transfer shaft and gears
steps.action: Install the transfer shaft and gears into the rear of the case.

mistakes.title: Transfer gears not fully seated
mistakes.what: Leaves the transfer shaft and gears short of their bearing seats.
mistakes.consequence: The extension case won't sit flat, or bearing preload is wrong once it is pulled down.
mistakes.prevent: Check the transfer assembly is fully home before fitting the transfer clutch.

steps.title: Install the transfer clutch
steps.action: Fit the transfer clutch hub, then the drum, turning the drum until it drops fully onto its splines.

mistakes.title: Transfer drum not fully engaged
mistakes.what: Leaves the transfer clutch drum on top of its splines.
mistakes.consequence: The extension case clamps the drum, so the AWD binds or the housing won't go on.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the transfer drum until it drops fully onto its splines.

mistakes.title: Cutting the hub sealing ring
mistakes.what: Forces the transfer clutch hub onto its shaft.
mistakes.consequence: The hub sealing ring is cut and the AWD clutch loses apply pressure.
mistakes.prevent: Lubricate the hub sealing ring and rotate the hub on gently.

steps.title: Refit the parking pawl
steps.action: Install the parking pawl, its spring and the pivot shaft.

mistakes.title: Pawl spring hooked wrong
mistakes.what: Installs the parking pawl spring in the wrong position.
mistakes.consequence: The pawl doesn't retract and grinds on the park gear while driving, or Park won't hold.
mistakes.prevent: Match the teardown photo and check the pawl snaps back freely when pushed in.

steps.title: Place the transfer gear shims
steps.action: Put each transfer shim set back in its own location, or measure and select new shims if bearings or cases were replaced.
steps.mistake: Swapping the two shim sets, which ruins transfer bearing preload.

mistakes.title: Swapping the transfer shim sets
mistakes.what: Puts each transfer shim set in the other's location.
mistakes.consequence: Transfer bearing preload is wrong, giving noise and early bearing failure.
mistakes.prevent: Fit each labelled transfer shim set in its own bore; the different diameters are your check.

mistakes.title: Reusing shims after new bearings
mistakes.what: Refits the old transfer shims after replacing transfer bearings or a case.
mistakes.consequence: The new parts change the stack height, so transfer preload is wrong.
mistakes.prevent: Measure and select new transfer shims whenever bearings or cases change.

mistakes.title: Shim falls out on assembly
mistakes.what: Lets a transfer shim drop out of position as the extension case goes on.
mistakes.consequence: Transfer end play is wrong and the extension case has to come off again.
mistakes.prevent: Check each transfer shim is still in its bore just before the extension case seats.

steps.title: Install the extension case
steps.action: With a new transfer clutch O-ring and fresh sealant, fit the extension case and torque its bolts in a crossing pattern.

mistakes.title: Transfer feed O-ring missing
mistakes.what: Fits the extension case without a new transfer clutch feed O-ring.
mistakes.consequence: The AWD clutch loses apply pressure at the extension case joint.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the new feed O-ring and check it is still in place as the extension case goes on.

mistakes.title: Sealant across the feed port
mistakes.what: Runs the extension case sealant bead over the transfer clutch feed.
mistakes.consequence: The transfer clutch feed is restricted by sealant, so the AWD clutch applies weakly or late.
mistakes.prevent: Keep the extension case bead clear of the feed port and every other opening.

mistakes.title: Drawing the housing down with bolts
mistakes.what: Uses the bolts to pull down an extension case that won't sit flush by hand.
mistakes.consequence: The housing cracks or a transfer shim or bearing is crushed.
mistakes.prevent: Find out why the extension case won't sit flat before tightening anything.

steps.title: Air-check the clutch circuits
steps.action: Apply low-pressure shop air to the forward and reverse feeds with the manual valve in D and then R, and to the transfer clutch port, listening for a clean apply.

mistakes.title: Skipping the air checks
mistakes.what: Closes the unit up without air-checking the clutch circuits.
mistakes.consequence: A cut ring or rolled seal is found only after installation, which means another teardown.
mistakes.prevent: Air-check the forward, reverse and transfer circuits before the pump and covers go on.

mistakes.title: Wrong manual valve position
mistakes.what: Air-checks the forward and reverse feeds without the manual valve in D and R.
mistakes.consequence: No apply is heard, giving a false failure or a false pass on the clutch circuits.
mistakes.prevent: Move the manual valve to D for the forward check and to R for the reverse check.

steps.title: Install the oil pump
steps.action: Fit the pump with new suction and pressure O-rings, torque its bolts, then install the pump drive chain and sprockets together.

mistakes.title: Swapping pump port O-rings
mistakes.what: Puts the small O-ring on the pump suction port and the large on the output.
mistakes.consequence: The pump draws air or leaks pressure, giving noise, low pressure and a risk of slip.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the large O-ring on the suction port and the small one on the output port.

mistakes.title: Uneven pump bolt torque
mistakes.what: Tightens the four pump mounting bolts one at a time.
mistakes.consequence: The pump body distorts against its mounting face and the pump gears bind.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten the pump mounting bolts evenly in stages and turn the pump drive after.

mistakes.title: Fitting pump sprockets separately
mistakes.what: Installs the pump drive sprockets one at a time and then tries to fit the chain.
mistakes.consequence: The chain is forced on and the sprockets or chain are damaged.
mistakes.prevent: Fit the pump drive chain and both sprockets together as one assembly.

steps.title: Replace the stator seal ring
steps.action: Fit a new plastic sealing ring on the stator support and oil it with CVTF.
steps.why: Subaru lists this ring as one-time-use.
steps.mistake: Reusing the old ring because it looks undamaged.

mistakes.title: Reusing the stator sealing ring
mistakes.what: Refits the old plastic stator support ring because it looks undamaged.
mistakes.consequence: Subaru lists it as one-time-use; a reused ring may not seal, and the CVT has to come out again to replace it.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new stator support sealing ring every time the chain cover is off.

mistakes.title: Fitting the ring dry
mistakes.what: Installs the new stator support ring without lubricating it.
mistakes.consequence: The dry ring can be damaged when the converter hub slides over it.
mistakes.prevent: Lubricate the stator support ring thoroughly with CVTF, as Subaru specifies.

steps.title: Bead sealant on chain cover
steps.action: Run a small bead of liquid gasket along the chamfer edge of the cover, skipping the marked oil hole.
steps.why: Sealant in the marked hole blocks oil flow, and too much squeezes into the case.
steps.mistake: Laying sealant around the marked oil hole or using too heavy a bead.

mistakes.title: Sealant around the marked hole
mistakes.what: Runs the chain cover bead around the oil hole Subaru marks.
mistakes.consequence: Sealant squeezes into the marked oil hole and blocks or restricts the oil flow it carries.
mistakes.prevent: Skip the marked hole as the bulletin shows, breaking the bead there.

mistakes.title: Too much chain cover sealant
mistakes.what: Lays a heavy bead on the chain cover.
mistakes.consequence: Excess chain cover sealant squeezes into the case, where crumbs can block oil passages.
mistakes.prevent: Use a small bead that just fills the chamfer once the cover is fitted.

mistakes.title: Bead off the chamfer
mistakes.what: Runs the bead on the flat face rather than along the chamfer edge.
mistakes.consequence: The extra seal the sealant forms in the chamfer is missing and seepage returns.
mistakes.prevent: Apply the bead along the chamfer edge of the cover, as Subaru's illustration shows.

mistakes.title: Using generic RTV
mistakes.what: Uses a general-purpose silicone in place of the specified ThreeBond 1215.
mistakes.consequence: The joint can seep again, which is the very failure the bulletin repairs.
mistakes.prevent: Use ThreeBond 1215, the sealant Subaru specifies for this joint.

steps.title: Torque the chain cover
steps.action: Fit the cover and tighten its ten bolts in a crossing pattern.

mistakes.title: Wrong cover torque pattern
mistakes.what: Tightens the chain cover bolts around in a circle or with an impact gun.
mistakes.consequence: The cover distorts and the bead is squeezed unevenly, leading to seepage.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten the chain cover bolts in a crossing pattern with a torque wrench.

mistakes.title: Using the TR690 torque value
mistakes.what: Uses the TR690's chain cover torque from the same bulletin.
mistakes.consequence: The TR580 cover is over-tightened, distorting the aluminum cover and squeezing the bead thin.
mistakes.prevent: Use 21 N·m for the TR580's ten equal-length bolts, not the TR690 value.

steps.title: Refit rod and shift linkage
steps.action: Install the parking rod, the manual shaft linkage and a new roll pin in the shift rail.

mistakes.title: Reusing the roll pin
mistakes.what: Refits the old roll pin in the shift rail.
mistakes.consequence: The pin works loose and the linkage gets sloppy, so range selection drifts.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new roll pin in the shift rail and check it sits flush on both sides.

mistakes.title: Park rod not under the pawl
mistakes.what: Fits the parking rod without its end in position against the pawl.
mistakes.consequence: Park doesn't engage and the car can roll away when left in P.
mistakes.prevent: Move the lever to P and check the output shaft locks before the pan goes on.

steps.title: Install the inhibitor switch
steps.action: Bolt the inhibitor switch on loosely, set it to the neutral position and tighten it.

mistakes.title: Range switch not set in neutral
mistakes.what: Tightens the inhibitor switch without aligning it in neutral.
mistakes.consequence: The car may not start in P or N, range signals disagree and codes set.
mistakes.prevent: Set the inhibitor switch in its neutral position, then tighten its bolts.

steps.title: Fit baffle and new strainer
steps.action: Bolt the pan baffle back on, then install a new oil strainer with a new O-ring.

mistakes.title: Reusing the old strainer
mistakes.what: Refits the original oil strainer.
mistakes.consequence: Trapped debris restricts flow, so the pump starves and pressure drops.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new strainer with a new O-ring whenever the unit is opened.

mistakes.title: Pinched strainer O-ring
mistakes.what: Pushes the new strainer in with its O-ring pinched or rolled.
mistakes.consequence: The pump draws air, giving noise, low pressure and a risk of chain slip.
mistakes.prevent: Lubricate the strainer O-ring and push the strainer straight into its bore.

steps.title: Install the oil pan
steps.action: Clean the magnet, fit the pan with a new gasket or sealant and a new drain plug gasket, and torque the bolts.

mistakes.title: Dirty magnet refitted
mistakes.what: Puts the pan back without cleaning the magnet.
mistakes.consequence: Old debris confuses the next inspection and can wash loose into the fluid.
mistakes.prevent: Clean the pan magnet and set it back in its place before the pan goes on.

mistakes.title: Uneven pan bolt torque
mistakes.what: Over-tightens or tightens the pan bolts unevenly.
mistakes.consequence: The pan flange distorts between bolts and leaks along the pan rail.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten the pan bolts evenly in a crossing pattern without over-tightening.

mistakes.title: Reusing the drain plug gasket
mistakes.what: Refits the pan drain plug with its old gasket.
mistakes.consequence: The flattened old gasket no longer seals and the drain plug weeps.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new drain plug gasket each time the plug comes out.

steps.title: Install the control valve body
steps.action: Put new O-rings in the case ports, set the valve body on level and run its bolts down evenly, with every solenoid ground back under its bolt.
steps.mistake: Doubling up old and new port O-rings, which holds the valve body off the case.

mistakes.title: Doubled port O-rings
mistakes.what: Fits new valve body port O-rings on top of old ones left in the case.
mistakes.consequence: The valve body is held off the case and pressure leaks between them.
mistakes.prevent: Confirm the case bores are empty before the new valve body O-rings go in.
mistakes.detect: The valve body rocks before the bolts are tightened.

mistakes.title: Missing port O-ring
mistakes.what: Leaves one valve body port O-ring out.
mistakes.consequence: That circuit leaks at the case, giving low pressure and slip.
mistakes.prevent: Count both valve body O-rings in before lowering the valve body.

mistakes.title: Solenoid ground left off
mistakes.what: Leaves a solenoid ground lead out from under its bolt.
mistakes.consequence: Solenoid codes set and the TCM may default to high line pressure.
mistakes.prevent: Check every solenoid ground against the teardown photos before the cover goes on.

mistakes.title: Uneven valve body bolts
mistakes.what: Runs each valve body bolt down fully one at a time.
mistakes.consequence: The valve body distorts against the case and valves stick in their bores.
mistakes.prevent: Snug all nine bolts, then tighten them evenly from the center out.

steps.title: Refit the top valve cover
steps.action: Reconnect the main harness connector and bolt the top cover back on.

mistakes.title: Connector not fully latched
mistakes.what: Pushes the main valve body connector on without hearing the latch.
mistakes.consequence: Intermittent codes set and the TCM falls back to failsafe pressure.
mistakes.prevent: Push the main connector home until it latches and tug-test it.

mistakes.title: Harness pinched under cover
mistakes.what: Bolts the top cover down with a lead under its edge.
mistakes.consequence: The trapped wire chafes through and shorts, setting solenoid circuit codes.
mistakes.prevent: Check the lead routing all round the cover edge before it goes down.

steps.title: Install the external sensors
steps.action: Fit the speed sensors and the secondary pressure sensor with new O-rings.

mistakes.title: Reusing sensor O-rings
mistakes.what: Refits the speed and pressure sensors with their old O-rings.
mistakes.consequence: The hardened old O-rings let the speed and pressure sensors seep CVTF.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new O-rings on every external sensor and oil them before fitting.

mistakes.title: Pressure sensor not latched
mistakes.what: Leaves the secondary pressure sensor connector not fully latched.
mistakes.consequence: P0841 sets soon after the rebuild from a poor secondary pressure sensor connection.
mistakes.prevent: Latch and tug-test the secondary pressure sensor connector.

steps.title: Fit new axle and front seals
steps.action: Drive in new differential side seals on both sides, then fit a new converter seal and stator shaft seal and oil the lips with CVTF.

mistakes.title: Driving seals in crooked
mistakes.what: Taps the new axle and front seals in without a driver.
mistakes.consequence: A cocked seal leaks around the axle or converter hub soon after the car is back on the road.
mistakes.prevent: Use a driver that bears on each seal's outer edge so it goes in square.

mistakes.title: Seal lips fitted dry
mistakes.what: Fits the converter and stator seals without oiling the lips.
mistakes.consequence: The dry converter and stator seal lips burn on first rotation and start to leak.
mistakes.prevent: Oil the converter and stator seal lips with CVTF before fitting.

mistakes.title: Swapping left and right seals
mistakes.what: Fits the left differential side seal on the right.
mistakes.consequence: Subaru lists separate left and right part numbers, so a swapped seal is a likely leak.
mistakes.prevent: Check the side seal part numbers and fit each one to its own side.

steps.title: Install the torque converter
steps.action: Slide the converter on while turning it until it drops through each spline engagement and sits fully back on the pump drive.
steps.why: A converter that is not fully home is pulled forward by the drive plate bolts and wrecks the pump drive.
steps.mistake: Bolting up with the converter sitting on the last spline instead of fully engaged.

mistakes.title: Converter not fully seated
mistakes.what: Bolts up with the converter on its last spline instead of fully engaged.
mistakes.consequence: The drive plate pulls the converter forward and damages the pump drive, hub and seal.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the converter until it drops through each engagement, and measure its set-back before mating.

mistakes.title: Cutting the seal with the hub
mistakes.what: Pushes the converter on at an angle.
mistakes.consequence: The new converter seal or stator sealing ring is cut and leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Slide the converter on straight while turning it, keeping the hub centered.

steps.title: Mate the CVT to the engine
steps.action: Raise the CVT on the jack, align it to the engine dowels and draw it in with the housing bolts, never with the converter nuts.

mistakes.title: Drawing in with the wrong fasteners
mistakes.what: Closes the gap between CVT and engine with the converter nuts or by forcing the housing bolts.
mistakes.consequence: The converter hub and pump drive are damaged, or the bell housing cracks.
mistakes.prevent: The housings must meet by hand on the dowels; find out why if they don't.

mistakes.title: Converter slid forward on install
mistakes.what: Tilts the CVT nose-down as it is raised on the jack.
mistakes.consequence: The converter slides forward off its engagement before the unit meets the engine.
mistakes.prevent: Keep the CVT level on the jack and check the converter set-back just before mating.

steps.title: Bolt converter to drive plate
steps.action: Rotate the engine and install the converter-to-drive-plate nuts to spec.

mistakes.title: Torquing one nut first
mistakes.what: Fully torques the first converter nut before starting the others.
mistakes.consequence: The converter is pulled off center against the drive plate, loading the hub and seal.
mistakes.prevent: Start every converter nut by hand, then torque them evenly in turn.

mistakes.title: Dropping a nut in the housing
mistakes.what: Lets a converter nut fall into the bell housing.
mistakes.consequence: It wedges between the drive plate and the housing and cracks the housing.
mistakes.prevent: Use a magnetic socket and account for every converter nut before turning the engine.

steps.title: Reconnect driveline and cooler
steps.action: Refit the crossmember, axles with new C-clips, propeller shaft, cooler lines and harness, flushing the cooler circuit first.
steps.why: Subaru treats the axle C-clips as one-time-use.

mistakes.title: Skipping the cooler flush
mistakes.what: Reconnects the cooler lines without flushing the cooler.
mistakes.consequence: Debris from the old failure is pumped into the rebuilt unit on first start.
mistakes.prevent: Flush the cooler whenever the pan held debris, the unit overheated or a failed unit is being replaced.

mistakes.title: Half-done cooler flush
mistakes.what: Uses the wrong product, or stops when it looks clear and doesn't blow out the residue.
mistakes.consequence: Debris or flush residue stays in the cooler and contaminates the new fluid.
mistakes.prevent: Use Subaru's cooler flush, repeat until it runs clean, then blow the cooler out with air.

mistakes.title: Cooler hoses badly clamped
mistakes.what: Refits the cooler hoses with clamps that aren't the factory type or aren't fully on.
mistakes.consequence: A cooler hose blows off, the CVT pumps out its fluid and the chain slips.
mistakes.prevent: Refit the cooler hoses with the factory clamps and check each one before filling.

mistakes.title: Reusing axle C-clips
mistakes.what: Refits the old axle C-clips.
mistakes.consequence: Subaru treats them as one-time-use; a weak clip lets the axle move in the differential.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new C-clips and pull-test each axle to confirm it is locked in.

mistakes.title: Dragging the axle across the seal
mistakes.what: Slides the axle spline in across the new side seal lip.
mistakes.consequence: The axle spline cuts the new side seal lip, which leaks gear oil from the first drive.
mistakes.prevent: Guide each axle in straight and keep the spline off the seal lip.

steps.title: Fill the front differential
steps.action: Fill the front differential with gear oil, not CVTF, and refit its plug.
steps.mistake: Filling the differential with CVTF, or the CVT with gear oil.

mistakes.title: Fluid swapped between compartments
mistakes.what: Fills the differential with CVTF or the CVT with gear oil.
mistakes.consequence: The hypoid gears wear in thin fluid, or the CVT needs a full drain and flush.
mistakes.prevent: Identify the differential fill and the CVT filler plug before opening either.

mistakes.title: Differential level guessed
mistakes.what: Fills the differential by pouring a quantity without checking the level.
mistakes.consequence: Too low wears the gears and bearings; too high leaks at the side seals.
mistakes.prevent: Use the capacity as a guide only and fill the differential to its level.

mistakes.title: Wrong gear oil grade
mistakes.what: Uses a differential oil that is not 75W-90 GL-5.
mistakes.consequence: The hypoid gears are not protected as intended and wear faster.
mistakes.prevent: Use 75W-90 GL-5 gear oil, as the sources list for this differential.

steps.title: Add the initial CVTF fill
steps.action: Fill the CVT through the filler plug with the specified fluid, temporarily refit the plug and start the engine.

spec.note: Green, for non-turbo TR580. Dry fill is roughly 12 L; the hot level check sets the final amount

steps.mistake: Using High Torque CVTF (meant for TR690 units such as the Forester XT) or a generic CVT fluid.

mistakes.title: Wrong CVT fluid
mistakes.what: Uses High Torque CVTF meant for TR690 units such as the Forester XT, a generic CVT fluid, or ATF.
mistakes.consequence: Subaru warns other fluids cause malfunction; noise, slip and unit failure follow.
mistakes.prevent: Use Subaru CVTF II for the non-turbo TR580 and nothing else.

mistakes.title: Choosing fluid by colour
mistakes.what: Grabs any green Subaru CVT fluid, including later low-viscosity types meant for other units.
mistakes.consequence: The wrong fluid for this unit brings performance problems and can lead to failure.
mistakes.prevent: Check the part number against Subaru's recommended materials for the 2014 to 2018 Forester non-turbo.

mistakes.title: Starting with too little fluid
mistakes.what: Starts the engine before enough fluid is in.
mistakes.consequence: The pump draws air, secondary pressure is low and the chain can slip.
mistakes.prevent: Put in close to the dry-fill amount before the first start.

mistakes.title: Filling by volume alone
mistakes.what: Pours in the overhaul capacity and calls the job done.
mistakes.consequence: The capacity is approximate, so the unit ends up over or under its true level.
mistakes.prevent: Use the volume as a starting point only and set the final level hot.

steps.title: Warm to check temperature
steps.action: Idle the engine and watch the CVTF temperature on the scan tool until it reaches the check window.

spec.note: 95–113 °F, read on the Subaru Select Monitor

steps.mistake: Checking the level cold, which leaves the CVT overfilled.

mistakes.title: Setting the level cold
mistakes.what: Adds fluid to the bottom of the filler hole with the fluid cold.
mistakes.consequence: Subaru warns a cold fill to the hole overfills the CVT and fluid spills out.
mistakes.prevent: Warm the CVTF into the check window before adding fluid to the hole.

mistakes.title: Overshooting the temperature window
mistakes.what: Idles the engine past the window before checking.
mistakes.consequence: Fluid expands with heat, so a level set too hot leaves the CVT short of fluid.
mistakes.prevent: Watch the scan tool and set the level while the CVTF is inside the window.

mistakes.title: Guessing fluid temperature
mistakes.what: Judges CVTF temperature from the coolant gauge or by touching the pan.
mistakes.consequence: The real fluid temperature is unknown and the level is set wrong.
mistakes.prevent: Read the CVTF temperature on the scan tool, not the coolant gauge.

steps.title: Circulate the new fluid
steps.action: Still idling with the brake held, move the lever slowly from P to R to N to D and back to P to push fluid through every circuit.

mistakes.title: Skipping the lever cycle
mistakes.what: Checks the level straight after start-up without cycling P-R-N-D and back.
mistakes.consequence: Circuits and pistons are not yet full, so the level reads high and the unit ends up low.
mistakes.prevent: Cycle the lever slowly through every range and back, engine idling, before checking.

steps.title: Set level at the filler hole
steps.action: With the engine idling, remove the filler plug, add fluid until it just reaches the bottom of the hole, then refit the plug with a new gasket.
steps.why: The level is only correct with the engine running and the fluid in the temperature window.

mistakes.title: Checking with the engine off
mistakes.what: Shuts the engine off before opening the filler plug.
mistakes.consequence: Fluid drains back from the circuits and the level reads high.
mistakes.prevent: Keep the engine idling the whole time the level is being set.

mistakes.title: Not rechecking an odd fill amount
mistakes.what: Adds far more or far less fluid than expected without rechecking conditions.
mistakes.consequence: The temperature or engine state was wrong, so the level is wrong too.
mistakes.prevent: Recheck that the CVTF is inside the window and the engine is running.

mistakes.title: Reusing the filler plug gasket
mistakes.what: Refits the filler plug with its old gasket.
mistakes.consequence: The used gasket no longer crushes to seal and the filler plug seeps.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new filler plug gasket every time, as Subaru requires.

mistakes.title: Filler plug torque guessed
mistakes.what: Tightens the filler plug without a torque wrench.
mistakes.consequence: The aluminum case thread strips, or an under-tightened filler plug seeps.
mistakes.prevent: Torque the filler plug to 50 N·m with an 8 mm hex bit and a new gasket.

spec.note: Filler plug, 36.9 ft·lb, new gasket, 8 mm hex

steps.title: Clear stored trouble codes
steps.action: Clear the codes, cycle the key and confirm no solenoid or sensor codes return.

mistakes.title: Calling it fixed after clearing
mistakes.what: Clears the codes and doesn't recheck after a drive cycle.
mistakes.consequence: Faults that only set over a drive cycle are missed and the car comes back.
mistakes.prevent: Run a drive cycle after clearing and read the codes again.

mistakes.title: Learning with faults present
mistakes.what: Goes on to AT learning with codes still active.
mistakes.consequence: AT learning stops and tells you to fix the stored faults before it will run.
mistakes.prevent: Repair every active fault and clear its code before starting AT learning.

steps.title: Clear the AT learning data
steps.action: Run the scan tool's clear AT learning function, then switch off for at least 30 seconds and back on; the AT temp light should flash four times.
steps.why: Old learned values belong to the worn parts and must go before new learning.

mistakes.title: Skipping the learning clear
mistakes.what: Runs AT learning with the old learned data still stored.
mistakes.consequence: The TCM keeps values learned on worn parts, giving harsh or slipping engagements and poor lock-up.
mistakes.prevent: Clear AT learning data first, then run the learning procedure.

mistakes.title: Not confirming the light flashes
mistakes.what: Doesn't watch for the AT temperature light to flash after key-on.
mistakes.consequence: A failed clear goes unnoticed and learning runs on old data.
mistakes.prevent: Watch for four flashes in two seconds and repeat the clear if they don't come.

mistakes.title: Key-off too short
mistakes.what: Turns the ignition back on before the minimum wait after the clear.
mistakes.consequence: The clear may not complete, leaving old learned values in place.
mistakes.prevent: Leave the ignition off for at least 30 seconds after the clear.

mistakes.title: Out-of-date TCM software
mistakes.what: Skips checking for a newer TCM calibration.
mistakes.consequence: Known fixes, such as the logic that clears solenoid contamination on the 2018 Forester, are missing.
mistakes.prevent: Check for a newer TCM calibration and reprogram before running learning.

mistakes.title: Reflashing on a sagging battery
mistakes.what: Reprograms the TCM without a stable power supply.
mistakes.consequence: A flash interrupted by battery discharge can ruin the TCM, and Subaru won't cover it.
mistakes.prevent: Connect the approved battery support unit in power supply mode while reprogramming.

steps.title: Prepare for AT learning
steps.action: Bring the CVTF into the learning window, select P, set the parking brake hard, lift the wheels clear and switch off electrical loads.

spec.note: 104–149 °F; keep the tires at least 30 cm off the ground

steps.mistake: Running learning with the fluid outside the temperature window, so it ends abnormally.

mistakes.title: Fluid outside the learning window
mistakes.what: Starts learning with the CVTF too cold or too hot.
mistakes.consequence: AT learning ends abnormally as soon as the fluid temperature drifts out of range.
mistakes.prevent: Bring the CVTF to 40 to 65 °C before starting learning.

mistakes.title: Tires too close to the ground
mistakes.what: Raises the car only slightly for learning.
mistakes.consequence: The car vibrates during learning and could touch down and move.
mistakes.prevent: Keep the tires at least 30 cm off the ground for learning.

mistakes.title: Loads on or brake weak
mistakes.what: Leaves lights, A/C or heaters on, or the parking brake not fully applied.
mistakes.consequence: AT learning ends abnormally partway through and has to start again from the beginning.
mistakes.prevent: Turn off every electrical load and set the parking brake hard.

steps.title: Run compulsory AT learning
steps.action: Start the compulsory learning mode in the scan tool's work support menu and follow the prompts until it reports a normal finish.
steps.why: The TCM must relearn clutch and pressure characteristics of the rebuilt parts.

mistakes.title: Touching pedals mid-learning
mistakes.what: Presses the accelerator or eases off the brake during learning.
mistakes.consequence: AT learning ends abnormally the moment the accelerator moves or the brake eases.
mistakes.prevent: Keep your feet as the scan tool prompts and touch nothing else.

mistakes.title: Accepting an abnormal end
mistakes.what: Drives off after the scan tool reports that learning ended abnormally.
mistakes.consequence: The TCM lacks learned values, so engagements are harsh or slipping.
mistakes.prevent: Start AT learning over from the beginning until it ends normally.

mistakes.title: Scan tool disconnected mid-learning
mistakes.what: Unplugs or powers down the scan tool during learning.
mistakes.consequence: A communication error stops learning and the lever may not shift.
mistakes.prevent: Keep the scan tool connected and powered until learning reports its end.

mistakes.title: Ignoring harsh engagement after learning
mistakes.what: Accepts hard garage shifts after learning finishes.
mistakes.consequence: The rebuilt clutches take the shock of every harsh engagement.
mistakes.prevent: Run the learning control pressure and extra learning procedures, then look for internal faults.

steps.title: Run torque converter relearn
steps.action: Perform the torque converter relearn procedure, especially if the valve body or converter was replaced.

mistakes.title: Skipping the converter relearn
mistakes.what: Leaves out the converter relearn after a valve body or converter change.
mistakes.consequence: Shudder when pulling away from or slowing to a stop can remain.
mistakes.prevent: Run the torque converter relearn and repeat it if the shudder persists.

mistakes.title: Swapping the valve body without data
mistakes.what: Replaces the valve body for shudder without the hot and cold lock-up comparison.
mistakes.consequence: The new valve body doesn't fix a shudder that has another cause.
mistakes.prevent: Compare lock-up duty hot and cold on decel to a stop, as Subaru's bulletin lays out.

steps.title: Stall-test D and R
steps.action: With the fluid hot, wheels chocked and brake held, hold full throttle for no more than 5 seconds in D, cool down in N for a minute, then repeat in R.

spec.note: D range; R range 1,900–2,650 rpm; CVTF at 60–80 °C (2017 Forester non-turbo)

mistakes.title: Holding stall too long
mistakes.what: Holds full throttle at stall beyond the limit.
mistakes.consequence: Engine oil and CVTF deteriorate and the forward clutch and reverse brake are damaged.
mistakes.prevent: Keep each stall test to no more than 5 seconds from closed throttle.

mistakes.title: No cool-down between stall tests
mistakes.what: Goes straight from the D stall test to the R test.
mistakes.consequence: Back-to-back stalls overheat the CVTF and the forward and reverse packs.
mistakes.prevent: Idle in P or N for at least a minute between stall tests.

mistakes.title: Stall test at wrong temperature
mistakes.what: Stall-tests with the CVTF outside the specified window.
mistakes.consequence: The stall speeds you read can't be compared with the published range.
mistakes.prevent: Bring the CVTF to 60 to 80 °C on the scan tool before the stall test.

mistakes.title: Pre-collision braking left on
mistakes.what: Leaves EyeSight pre-collision braking on during the stall test.
mistakes.consequence: The pre-collision system can brake or cut power and spoil the stall reading.
mistakes.prevent: Switch pre-collision braking off and keep everyone clear of the car.

steps.title: Road test the vehicle
steps.action: Drive and check engagements, smooth ratio change, lock-up, no flare or judder from a stop, and no binding on tight turns.

mistakes.title: A short, gentle road test
mistakes.what: Drives a few minutes with the fluid still cool.
mistakes.consequence: Faults that appear only hot are missed and the car comes back.
mistakes.prevent: Drive both cold and fully hot, slowing to a stop several times, and record data.

mistakes.title: Not testing tight turns
mistakes.what: Skips slow full-lock turns on dry pavement.
mistakes.consequence: A tight transfer clutch or AWD solenoid fault is missed until tires and driveline suffer.
mistakes.prevent: Make slow full-lock turns on dry pavement and check that all four tires match in size and wear.

mistakes.title: Hard launches straight away
mistakes.what: Uses full throttle or tows before the level is rechecked.
mistakes.consequence: If the fill is still low, a shock load from a hard launch can slip the chain.
mistakes.prevent: Drive gently, with no towing, until the level has been rechecked hot.

mistakes.title: Not logging pulley speeds
mistakes.what: Road-tests by feel only.
mistakes.consequence: Slight chain slip goes unnoticed on the road test until the damage grows.
mistakes.prevent: Log engine, primary and secondary pulley speeds and look for any mismatch.

steps.title: Recheck level and leaks
steps.action: Recheck the CVTF level in the temperature window and inspect the chain cover seam, axle seals and pan for leaks.

mistakes.title: Skipping the post-drive level check
mistakes.what: Doesn't recheck the CVTF level after the road test.
mistakes.consequence: Air purged from the circuits leaves the level low, which brings air noise and a risk of chain slip.
mistakes.prevent: Recheck the level in the temperature window after the road test.

mistakes.title: Mistaking fill spills for leaks
mistakes.what: Takes CVTF spilled during filling for a seal leak.
mistakes.consequence: A good reseal is condemned, or a real leak is hidden among the spills.
mistakes.prevent: Clean every surface after filling so any new leak is obvious.

mistakes.title: Not rechecking the cover seam
mistakes.what: Doesn't look at the chain cover seam after the unit has been hot.
mistakes.consequence: Seepage from a poor reseal is found by the customer instead.
mistakes.prevent: Inspect the chain cover seam after the unit has been hot and cooled.

failureModes.title: Chain slip and pulley face damage
failureModes.cause: Secondary (clamping) pressure falls, from low fluid, worn valve body bores, pressure sensor or solenoid faults, and the chain slips on the sheaves under load. Once it slips, chain and pulley faces are damaged together.
symptoms: Engine rpm flares without matching road speed
Primary and secondary pulley speeds that stop tracking each other on a data log
Fine steel on the pan magnet
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Judge chain and all four sheave faces as one decision and replace them as a set (tr580-042 to tr580-044); find and fix the pressure loss behind the slip in the valve body (tr580-051); set the level hot and recheck it after driving (tr580-104 to tr580-106, tr580-114).

failureModes.title: Lock-up solenoid opens when hot
failureModes.cause: The lock-up duty solenoid's coil goes open circuit as it heats, so the TCM loses control of converter lock-up.
symptoms: Code P2763 once the car is warm
No lock-up, or a lock-up feel coming to a stop
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Test the solenoid both cold and heated (tr580-050); replace the valve body or swap in a known-good solenoid with a soldered, oil-proof splice; check grounds and routing on reassembly (tr580-094, tr580-095).

failureModes.title: Converter clutch won't release
failureModes.cause: On early converters, wear of an internal thrust washer restricts the passage that bleeds off lock-up pressure. Subaru changed the washer to a needle bearing.
symptoms: Engine rpm drops very low when coming to a stop
Feels like stopping a manual car without the clutch
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Fit an updated or new converter rather than reusing an early or debris-filled one (tr580-049, tr580-098), and run the converter relearn (tr580-111).

failureModes.title: Valve body bore wear
failureModes.cause: The lube valve, TCC boost valve and forward/reverse regulating valve wear their bores, leaking secondary, TCC and clutch pressure to exhaust.
symptoms: Delayed forward and reverse, harsh reverse
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Decide the valve body on its bores, not its looks: fit Subaru's updated valve body or ream and fit oversize valve kits (tr580-051), and treat any burnt pack as a sign of this wear (tr580-046).

failureModes.title: Shudder and lock-up pressure codes
failureModes.cause: Valve sleeve wear in the control valve body upsets lock-up pressure control. Subaru released a valve body with an enhanced valve sleeve.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Fit the updated valve body (tr580-051), run the converter relearn (tr580-111), and road-test both cold and hot (tr580-113).

failureModes.title: CVTF seepage at the chain cover
failureModes.cause: The sealant on the oil pump chain cover and the original input shaft seal let CVTF seep out toward the converter housing.
symptoms: Wet, dirty CVTF trails at the bell housing
Fluid collecting at the low point of the converter case
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Pry only on the tabs (tr580-021), clean without abrasives or air (tr580-041), fit the redesigned seal flush (tr580-058), a new stator ring (tr580-087), and a small ThreeBond 1215 bead that skips the marked hole, torqued in a crossing pattern (tr580-088, tr580-089).

failureModes.title: Low or wrong fluid
failureModes.cause: A CVT left short of fluid (some 2017 Foresters left the factory that way) or filled with the wrong fluid cannot hold clamping pressure or friction properly.
symptoms: Chain slip on hard acceleration or hill climbing
Noise complaints after a fluid service
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Use Subaru CVTF II (tr580-103), set the level hot in the window with the lever cycled and engine idling (tr580-104 to tr580-106), and recheck after the road test (tr580-114).

failureModes.title: Secondary pressure sensor code P0841
failureModes.cause: Wiring or terminal faults, contamination in a fluid pressure solenoid, or a real internal pressure fault upsets the secondary pressure signal.
symptoms: Whining if a hard part has failed
Burnt fluid in the worst cases
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Follow the P0841 flow before swapping parts (tr580-052), latch the sensor connector (tr580-096), and load the latest TCM calibration before learning (tr580-108).

failureModes.title: Electrical faults forcing high pressure
failureModes.cause: Most sensor and solenoid circuit faults make the TCM command maximum secondary pressure, and some leave the ratio fixed.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Record codes before teardown (tr580-001), photograph routing and grounds (tr580-009), check solenoids and connectors (tr580-050, tr580-052), and refit every ground and connector carefully (tr580-094, tr580-095).

failureModes.title: AWD transfer clutch bind or slip
failureModes.cause: A tight or worn transfer clutch pack, a failing AWD solenoid, or mismatched tire sizes load the transfer clutch.
symptoms: Tight turns feel like the brakes are dragging
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Measure and set transfer clearance (tr580-063, tr580-064), air-test it in a press (tr580-065), refit the feed O-ring (tr580-084), and test tight turns with matched tires (tr580-113).

failureModes.title: Chain and guide wear noise
failureModes.cause: The chain wears and the plastic guides break up; a loose guide lets the chain rub the oil supply tubes until they wear and leak pressure.
symptoms: Guide plastic in the strainer or pan
Pressure loss from worn oil tubes
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Inspect chain and guides closely (tr580-042), release and lock guide tabs gently (tr580-028, tr580-075), and fit the anchor bolt.

failureModes.title: Cooler debris kills the new unit
failureModes.cause: Debris from the original failure stays in the cooler and lines and is pumped into the rebuilt or replacement unit.
symptoms: Early repeat failure after a rebuild or replacement
Fresh fluid darkens or carries metal soon after
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Cap the lines at removal (tr580-005) and flush the cooler with Subaru's flush until clean before reconnecting (tr580-101).

failureModes.title: Fluid breakdown and solenoid wear
failureModes.cause: Fluid left in service too long, especially in hard use, carries wear products that wear the valve body and solenoids.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Read the drained fluid (tr580-002), test every solenoid against its own range (tr580-050), and decide the valve body on its condition (tr580-051).

failureModes.title: Front differential wear
failureModes.cause: The front differential has its own gear oil; skipped changes, a quick-lube shop draining the wrong plug, or the wrong fluid wears the hypoid gears and bearings.
symptoms: Howl that changes with road speed
Metal on the differential plug magnet
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Drain and read the differential oil separately (tr580-003), inspect the final drive (tr580-053), and refill with 75W-90 GL-5 to level (tr580-102).

failureModes.title: Pulley shaft bearing noise
failureModes.cause: A pulley shaft bearing wears and becomes rough.
symptoms: Roughness felt when the pulley is turned by hand
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Check each bearing (tr580-045), press new ones on by the inner race and restake the nut (tr580-055), and recheck pulley shims (tr580-072).

failureModes.title: Forward clutch burn and late engagement
failureModes.cause: Low forward clutch pressure from a worn regulating valve bore, a rolled piston seal or a loose pack lets the forward clutch slip.
symptoms: Burnt friction material in the pan
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Reseal and stack the forward pack with soaked frictions and the cushion plate the right way (tr580-059), set its clearance (tr580-060), air-check it (tr580-085), and fix the regulating valve bore (tr580-051).
